text: The Patriots are marking a bittersweet week as Stephon Gilmore, the two-time All-Pro cornerback and 2019 NFL Defensive Player of the Year, returns to Foxborough on Friday, September 18, to retire as a member of New England on a one-day contract—a fitting sendoff for one of the franchise's most dominant defensive talents in recent memory. On the injury front, running back TreVeyon Henderson, who missed the Patriots' opener with an ankle injury, declared himself "ready to go" for Sunday's Week 2 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, a crucial piece for the offense as New England looks to bounce back. The Patriots organization is also turning its attention toward community recognition, hosting the 2026 Myra Kraft Community MVP Awards to honor 26 volunteers across all six New England states, with Susan Shaw winning the grand prize in a ceremony that celebrated the impact of grassroots service. Meanwhile, the Patriots are getting creative with their international promotion for this year's Munich game, enlisting Pro Football Hall of Famer Adam Vinatieri to attempt a Guinness World Record kick at Jungfraujoch in the Swiss Alps on Tuesday, September 22—a spectacle that underscores the organization's ambitious vision for bringing American football to Europe.
